title: Visualization of cortical microtubule networks in plant cells by live imaging and immunostaining
protocol: Melt MS medium using a microwave or use it directly if freshly autoclaved.
Add vitamins to the MS medium to achieve a final concentration of 1×.
Add BAP stock to the MS medium to reach a final concentration of 200 nM.
Pour the prepared ACM into Petri dishes (60 × 10 mm).
Choose plants with inflorescences approximately 2–3 cm high for further experiments.
Remove outer mature flowers using tweezers.
Cut the stem at about 1 cm length from the tip and insert it into ACM.
Dissect the plant further using fine-tipped tweezers, removing flowers carefully until reaching the desired floral stage.
Move the whole shoot apex to new ACM.
Insert the stem into the medium with an angle that makes the sepal primordium parallel to the surface.
Rehydrate the Petri dish with sterile water, ensuring the apex is under water.
Incubate for approximately 10 minutes.
Remove the water from the Petri dish.
Seal the Petri dish tightly.
Transfer the Petri dish to a growth chamber for recovery.
Dissect the vegetative shoot apex including as many roots as possible.
Wash plants grown in soil thoroughly with tap water before dissection.
Cut off old leaves using a needle from a 1 mL insulin syringe.
Remove leaf coverings around the shoot apical meristem using fine tweezers under high magnification of a stereo microscope to expose young leaf primordia (P1-P3).
Dissect flowers by cutting at the base of the pedicel close to the stem.
Pour sterile water into the Petri dish for dissection if necessary.
Culture the dissected shoot apex long-term to observe growth and CMT dynamics.
Use fine tweezers and a stereo microscope with high magnification for successful dissection.
Ensure a recovery period of at least 4 hours is provided.
Dilute the FM4-64 stock solution to a final concentration of 0.33 mg/mL.
Apply 5 μL of diluted FM4-64 on the flower bud using a micropipette.
Close the Petri dish and keep it in darkness for 5–10 minutes.
Rinse briefly with sterile water for two times.
Apply 5 μL propidium iodide solution to the flower bud using a micropipette.
Keep the Petri dish in darkness for 5–10 minutes.
Rinse briefly with sterile water for two times.

Clean the objectives of the upright confocal microscope LSM 700 (Zeiss) equipped with water immersion objectives with 70% ethanol before starting experiments using lens paper or high-purity cotton applicator.
Pour sterile water into the Petri dish to submerge the shoot apex.
Use a pipette to blow away any air bubble on the shoot apex.
Position the Petri dish on the stage center.
Mark the front position on the Petri dish using a marker (optional).
Use transmission light to find the flower bud.
Set up the pinhole size, laser power, gain, and offset.
Adjust the laser power to 2%–10% of 10 mW to avoid photo-bleaching and sample damage.
Set the pinhole size to 1 AU (Airy unit).
Use the range indicator to set gain and offset for optimal contrast and to avoid overexposure.
Select the frame size as 1,024 × 1,024 pixels which matches closely the diffraction-limited performance of the objectives.
Precisely optimize the frame size by clicking the “optimal” button in the ZEN software for calculation of appropriate number of pixels.
Ensure xy pixel dimensions are 114 μm.
Increase the signal-to-noise ratio using high scanning speed under line scanning mode with 3× averaging.
Acquire z stacks at intervals of 0.25–1 μm.
Use z steps of 0.5 μm for capturing CMT dynamics.
Capture volumetric temporal resolution sufficient for CMT dynamics.
Allow reasonable 3D reconstruction in periclinal walls.
Allow reasonable 3D reconstruction in anticlinal walls.
Remove water from the sample as much as possible after acquisition.
Cover the Petri dish with its lid and seal it.
Return the Petri dish to the growth chamber.
Clean the objective before each acquisition to avoid contamination.
Use a 63× objective for small younger sepal primordia.
Avoid over-sampling in z steps during acquisition to minimize photo-bleaching.
Avoid any air bubble between the objective and samples.
Image processing 3D reconstruction using Zeiss software (ZEN, black edition) with transparency rendering mode to visualize the CMT network in 3D.
Obtain surface renderings using MERRYPROJ or MorphoGraphX software.
Choose a subset of stack using ZEN software for visualizing CMT organization in anticlinal walls.
Make a 3D reconstruction and tilt the 3D image properly to show the anticlinal CMT networks.
Quantify CMT anisotropy using Fiji plugin—FibrilTool.
Prepare fixative by adding 4 g paraformaldehyde to 80 mL MTSB, dissolving with NaOH pellets, and adjusting pH to 7.0 with H2SO4.
Add 1 mL 50% glutaraldehyde to the solution.
Mix well and fill up to 100 mL with MTSB after adding 300 μL Tween 20 and 300 μL Triton X-100.
Seal the fixative during and after preparation due to paraformaldehyde's toxicity and tendency to evaporate.
Dissect tomato shoot apices under a dissecting microscope for tissue fixation.
Dig a hole in a 3% agar plate.
Vertically insert a tomato shoot apex from the tissue culture medium.
Remove leaves older than P3 using the needle from a 1 mL insulin syringe.
Incubate the dissected shoot apices in a 15 mL conical tube with 10 mL fixative.
Vacuum infiltrate at −0.075 MPa (550 mm Hg) for 10 min at room temperature (23°C–25°C).
Repeat vacuum infiltration for a total of 3 times (3 × 10 min).
Renew the fixative each time after vacuum infiltration.
Incubate in new fixative for an additional 3 h at room temperature (23°C–25°C) with the tube horizontally arranged.
Discard the fixative.
Incubate samples in MTSB for 20 min with the tube horizontally arranged.
Repeat incubation in MTSB for a total of 3 times (3 × 20 min).
Renew MTSB each time after incubation.
Prepare 6% low melting agarose by adding 1.8 g low melting agarose to 30 mL ddH2O.
Heat the mixture to dissolve in a water bath at 96°C.
Cool down the melted agarose to approximately 40°C before tissue embedding.
Pour fixed samples of tomato shoot apices into a 6 cm Petri dish together with MTSB.
Set a hot plate to 37°C.
Place a 44 × 44 × 7 mm plastic weighing dish on the hot plate.
Fill the dish with melted agarose (∼8–10 mL per plate).
Use tweezers to place samples into the melted agarose, adjusting their orientation as needed.
Transfer the weighing dish to 4°C and let stand for 15 minutes until the agarose solidifies.
Take a poly-L-lysine coated glass slide.
Draw a circle on the slice using a PAP pen.
Fill the circle with MTSB.
Cut an agarose block containing an individual tomato shoot apex with a razor blade.
Trim the agarose block to an appropriate size for use in a vibratome.
Fix the trimmed agarose block onto the specimen disc using cyanoacrylate adhesive (e.g., 502 super glue).
Apply adhesive evenly to the vertical faces of the block.
Fill the cooling bath with ice and fill the buffer tray with 1× PBS.
Make agarose sections of 40–50 μm thickness with sectioning speed at 0.65–0.78 mm/s and the sectioning frequency as 40 Hz.
Pick up sections using a brush and load them into the MTSB in the PAP circle.
Put slides with sections in a humid box.
Apply adhesive to the vertical faces of the block to make sections visible.
Wait a few seconds after drawing with the PAP pen to let the mark dry before adding MTSB.
Draw the PAP-rectangles which can cover a larger area of the slide for collecting multiple sections from one individual sample.
Prepare the enzymatic solution with 1% (w/v) hemicellulose and 1% (v/v) Triton X-100 in MTSB.
Replace MTSB in the PAP circle with the enzymatic solution using a pipettor.
Incubate sections in the enzymatic solution for 15 minutes at room temperature (23°C–25°C).
Remove the enzymatic solution from the slices.
Wash sections three times with 1× TBS for 5 minutes each without shaking.
Prepare the primary antibody solution by diluting mouse anti-α-tubulin antibody in 1× TBS containing 1% (w/v) BSA at a 1:800 dilution.
Remove 1× TBS from the slides.
Apply 200 μL of primary antibody solution per slide.
Incubate the slides in a humid box for overnight (12–16 hours) at 4°C.
Transfer samples to room temperature (23°C–25°C).
Remove primary antibody solution from the slides.
Wash sections with 1× TBS three times for 10 min each by incubation without shaking.
Dilute Alexa Fluor 488 conjugated donkey anti-mouse IgG in 1× TBS containing 1% (w/v) BSA at a 1:500 dilution.
Remove 1× TBS from the slides and apply 200 μL secondary antibody solution per slide.
Incubate the slides in a humid box for 2 h at 37°C in the dark.
Remove secondary antibody solution from the slides.
Wash sections with 1× TBS three times for 10 min each by incubation without shaking.
Apply 200 μL 1 μg/mL DAPI per slide.
Incubate for 15 min at room temperature (23°C–25°C) in the dark.
Remove DAPI solution and incubate sections in 1× TBS for 10 min.
Remove 1× TBS from the slices.
Mount the slide with ProLong Gold antifade reagent.
Cover the slide with a coverslip.
Use a 488 nm laser for excitation of Alexa Fluor 488.
Collect emission at 500–530 nm.
Set laser power to 10 mW.
Set pinhole size to 1.2 AU (30.7 μm).
Use a 405 nm laser for excitation of DAPI.
Collect emission at 425–475 nm.
Set laser power to 10 mW.
Set pinhole size to 1.2 AU (30.7 μm).
Set scanning step to 0.5 μm.
Perform maxima z-projection on generated stacks to obtain CMT organization.
Use a 100× oil objective for higher resolution visualization of CMTs in Arabidopsis cells.
Perform microscopy immediately after mounting the slides to prevent signal fading and depolymerization of CMTs.
